chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The contracted slave inherits and is inherited from, according to the portion of the manumission price he has paid off.

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبُ: A slave who has contracted with their master to pay a fixed sum for their freedom
key_terms.يُورَثُ: Is inherited from (passes an estate to heirs)

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed for a slave who has contracted for their freedom?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the unique legal status of the mukatab, establishing that their inheritance rights are proportional to the portion of the manumission price they have already settled, distinguishing them from both fully enslaved persons and free individuals. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that the mukatab possesses a 'partial free' status, allowing them to accumulate and transmit wealth as they progress toward full emancipation. This mechanism ensures economic fairness by linking inheritance shares directly to the degree of financial independence achieved.
